title: attest.py has no retraction verb, so a false act is permanent and uncorrectable
description:
FOUND BY HITTING IT, on 2026-08-17, during T-400. This is not a hypothetical.

WHAT HAPPENED. The coordinator smoke-tested the new D3a intent path against the live
registry and signed, as revision-doctrina, an act with kind=verdict and ref=T-376. NO
VERDICT ON T-376 WAS RENDERED. The ref was chosen carelessly. So a signed, verified,
fully-anchored act now sits on a real name's chain asserting a verdict that does not exist,
and trace() reports it as COMPLETE, which it truthfully is.

WHY IT IS STILL THERE. Removal was attempted and correctly refused twice:
prevent_data_loss.py blocked it, and safe_delete.py refused .harness/acts/ as a
control-plane path. Those refusals are RIGHT and must not be relaxed -- an agent that can
erase the evidentiary record has no evidentiary record. A direct filesystem call that would
have bypassed both was available and deliberately not used.

THE GAP. attest.py's contest() docstring already admits it: 'that is a retraction, which is
a different verb and does not exist yet'. So the ONLY correction available was to sign a
kind=filing act (seq 2 on that chain) recording that seq 1 is void. That correction is weak
in three specific ways, and each is a design question rather than a bug to patch:
  1. It sits AFTER the act it corrects and nothing links them mechanically. A reader who
     fetches seq 1 alone sees a verdict and no hint that seq 2 exists.
  2. It carries no more authority than the act it corrects. Same key, same name. Under D-17
     a forger can file a false verdict AND a false retraction of a true one.
  3. verify_name and trace do not know the concept exists, so a retracted act still reports
     as complete and verified.

WHAT TO DECIDE FIRST, before writing code. Whether a retraction is (a) a chained act that
verify and trace must consult when reporting an earlier act, or (b) an adjudication only a
DISTINCT name can make, which would align it with PR-015's confirmation floor and with
producer != approver. Option (b) is stronger and slower. The coordinator has no view worth
recording here.

DO NOT let a retraction verb become a deletion verb. The record stays append-only. A
retraction adds; it never removes. If the design starts wanting to remove, that is the
signal it went wrong.

PR-022 clause 4 applies throughout: a retraction must attach NO consequence to anyone.
acceptance_criteria: A written decision on whether a retraction is a chained self-act or an adjudication by a distinct name, with the reasoning, BEFORE any code.
The record stays append-only: nothing in the design removes or rewrites an act. A design that removes is a wrong answer, not a faster one.
verify_name and trace must consult retractions when reporting the retracted act, or the design must say explicitly why they should not.
The three named weaknesses of the seq-2 filing workaround are each addressed or each explicitly accepted with a reason.
revision-doctrina seq 1 (the false verdict on T-376) is the acceptance case: after the change, a reader of seq 1 alone must learn it is void.
PR-022 clause 4: the retraction attaches no consequence to any name. State it and pin it.
D-17 stated: a forger can file a false retraction of a true act, and the design does not prevent that.

notes.note:
T-406 DECIDIDO ANTES DE CUALQUIER CODIGO, como pedia el criterio 1. La retraccion es un
ACTO ENCADENADO REFLEXIVO, y la opcion (b) no es mas fuerte: es un error de categoria.

NO SE PUEDE RETRACTAR LA AFIRMACION DE OTRO. Una retraccion es un hablante desconociendo su
propia afirmacion. Lo que hace un tercero con una afirmacion que cree falsa es CONTESTARLA, y
`attest.py contest` ya existe, presenta el reclamo como acto firmado en la cadena DEL ACUSADOR y
vuelve una acusacion falsa permanentemente atribuible a quien la presento (AF-3). Construir una
'retraccion' de segunda parte duplicaria contest bajo un nombre que la describe mal, y la
describe mal en la direccion peligrosa: 'retractado' se lee como EL AUTOR SE DESDIJO cuando
significaria ALGUIEN MAS LO DISPUTA.

CONSECUENCIA DE ELEGIR REFLEXIVO: la retraccion esta disponible de INMEDIATO, sin esperar a un
segundo. Esa es la direccion correcta de falla. En cualquier hueco donde un acto falso conocido
queda sin desconocer, trace lo reporta COMPLETE. Mas lento no es mas seguro cuando lo que se
retrasa es la correccion.

LAS TRES DEBILIDADES DEL PARCHE seq-2, cada una atendida:
  1. VA DESPUES Y NADA LAS LIGA -- RESUELTO. El cuerpo carga `retracts: <digest del acto
     objetivo>`, la misma forma de campo-digest que ya usa `intent`. La resolucion es HACIA
     ATRAS: al reportar el acto N, la herramienta recorre la cadena de ese nombre buscando un
     acto cuyo `retracts` sea el digest de N. Sin indice, sin cache, sin segundo registro -- el
     defecto del cache de roster.py es exactamente lo que no se repite. Cuatro negativas:
     objetivo en la propia cadena; objetivo existente y verificable; una sola retraccion por
     objetivo; y UNA RETRACCION NO SE PUEDE RETRACTAR (des-desconocer no es un acto de habla que
     la cadena pueda representar con honestidad, y permitirlo abre un vaiven sin estado final).
  2. NO CARGA MAS AUTORIDAD QUE EL ACTO QUE CORRIGE -- ACEPTADA CON RAZON. Misma llave, mismo
     nombre. Bajo D-17 esto no tiene arreglo dentro del arnes y un diseno que dijera arreglarlo
     estaria reclamando un limite que no existe. Lo que lo vuelve soportable es DIS-2, que ya
     gobierna cada acto del modulo: EL CREDITO SIGUE A LA FIRMA, SIEMPRE. Una retraccion forjada
     firmada como A se acredita a A. Forjar puede destruir; nunca puede enriquecer.
  3. verify_name Y trace NO CONOCEN EL CONCEPTO -- RESUELTO. Las filas de trace ganan
     `retracted` y `retracted_by`. `complete` CONSERVA su significado -- es sobre el camino de
     anclaje, y un acto retractado puede tener ese camino completo -- asi que una fila
     retractada lee complete: true, retracted: true, que es la verdad: bien firmado, bien
     anclado, y desconocido. Colapsarlos destruiria informacion. Conteos crudos y distintos.

CASO DE ACEPTACION: revision-doctrina seq 1, kind=verdict ref=T-376. EL LIMITE, NOMBRADO EN VEZ
DE MAQUILLADO: quien haga cat del archivo 001.json sigue viendo un veredicto. El archivo es
inmutable y tiene que seguir siendolo -- esa es justo la propiedad que se protege. Lo que el
diseno garantiza es que TODA HERRAMIENTA que reporte seq 1 reporte la retraccion junto con el:
trace, verify, chain y los renderizadores. Quien rodea las herramientas rodea la resolucion,
igual que quien rodea warrant.py rodea la verificacion del warrant.

CLAUSULA 4 DE PR-022: la retraccion no ata NINGUNA consecuencia a ningun nombre. No baja
standing, no cierra un privilegio, no alimenta ninguna cifra citable. Cambia una sola cosa: lo
que las herramientas de reporte dicen de un acto. Se fija con una prueba que verifica LA SALIDA
y no solo los nombres del codigo (T-410).

D-17 DECLARADO: un forjador puede presentar una retraccion falsa de un acto verdadero, y este
diseno no lo impide.

EL REGISTRO SIGUE SIENDO SOLO-AGREGAR. Nada en el diseno elimina ni reescribe un acto. Si la
implementacion empieza a querer eliminar, esa es la senal de que salio mal, y las guardas que
rehusaron la eliminacion el 2026-08-17 se quedan igual de estrictas.

VERIFIED via code read of attest.py contest()/PRIVILEGED_KINDS/INTENT_KIND (cognitive
diversity: the producer's method was textual/design reasoning; I verified by independently
executing/reading the actual attest.py source rather than trusting the doc's characterization).

CENTRAL ATTACK -- "distinct-name retraction is a category error because contest already
covers it": CONFIRMED TRUE by code read. attest.py contest() (line 1077-1099):
  if accuser == target_name:
      raise AttestError("a name cannot contest its own act; that is a retraction, "
                        "which is a different verb and does not exist yet")
contest() is mechanically restricted to a DISTINCT accuser disputing another name's act, files
the claim on the ACCUSER's own chain, and its body already carries
  "AF_3": "this claim is permanently attributable to the filing name, whether or not it is
  upheld"
-- exactly matching the design's description. So "option (b), a distinct-name adjudication"
literally already exists under a different, correctly-scoped name; building a second-party
"retraction" would duplicate contest. The design's argument holds.

Supporting claims checked against code:
- PRIVILEGED_KINDS = frozenset({"verdict", "contest", "distinguish", "grant"}) -- confirmed at
  attest.py:144. "retract" is correctly absent, consistent with the design proposing it
  unprivileged.
- INTENT_KIND absent from PRIVILEGED_KINDS "for the same reason" (regress) -- confirmed,
  attest.py:161 docstring reads near-verbatim: "INTENT_KIND is deliberately absent. An intent
  requiring an intent is an infinite regress."
- git status/diff on attest.py, warrant.py, precedent.py: NO CHANGES. Confirms "no source
  edits" claim and that this is a design doc only (thinker role respected).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (7/7 met):
1. Decision stated before code, with reasoning -- yes.
2. Append-only preserved; nothing removes/rewrites an act -- yes, stated explicitly plus a
   dedicated "what must not happen" section.
3. verify_name/trace consult retractions -- yes, both specified (trace rows gain
   retracted/retracted_by; verify_name reports retraction alongside signature verdict without
   invalidating the signature).
4. Three named weaknesses: #1 fixed (backward `retracts:<digest>` resolution, no side index,
   4 named refusals including "a retraction cannot be retracted"); #2 explicitly ACCEPTED with
   reason (D-17 is unfixable in-harness; DIS-2 credit-follows-signature is the mitigation, and
   the doc states plainly "this design does not prevent that"); #3 fixed (trace/verify_name
   consult retractions, complete vs. retracted kept as separate booleans rather than collapsed
   -- correctly reasoned, since complete is about the anchoring walk, a fact independent of
   disownment).
5. Acceptance case (revision-doctrina seq 1): addressed, and the limit is NAMED not glossed --
   the doc states explicitly that `cat .harness/acts/revision-doctrina/001.json` directly still
   shows a verdict (immutability preserved), and the guarantee is scoped to "every TOOL that
   reports seq 1" (trace/verify/chain/renderers), which is the correct and honestly-bounded
   claim.
6. PR-022 clause 4 pinned: yes, quoted, and a test proposal (output-shape guard) is specified.
7. D-17 stated as a real, unclosed limit: yes, verbatim in the doc.

No fatal miscitation, no widening of any guardrail, thinker-role respected (no source edits).

ACCEPT.
